subject: dbms
title: Select All Employees
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list the name and salary of every employee.
sampleSolution: SELECT name, salary FROM Employees;
explanation: A plain SELECT with the two requested columns, no filtering needed.

subject: dbms
title: Employees Earning More Than 50000
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list the names of employees whose salary is greater than 50000.
sampleSolution: SELECT name FROM Employees WHERE salary > 50000;
explanation: WHERE filters individual rows before any aggregation, comparing salary directly to the literal.

subject: dbms
title: Employees Hired After a Date
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list all employees hired after '2022-01-01', ordered by hire_date ascending.
sampleSolution: SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE hire_date > '2022-01-01' ORDER BY hire_date ASC;
explanation: WHERE filters by date comparison; ORDER BY hire_date ASC sorts the results chronologically.

subject: dbms
title: Count Total Employees
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to return the total number of employees.
sampleSolution: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_employees FROM Employees;
explanation: COUNT(*) counts every row in the table regardless of NULLs in any particular column.

subject: dbms
title: Average Salary
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to return the average salary of all employees.
sampleSolution: SELECT AVG(salary) AS avg_salary FROM Employees;
explanation: AVG() computes the mean of the salary column across all rows.

subject: dbms
title: Count Employees per Department
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to return each department's id and the number of employees in it.
sampleSolution: SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM Employees GROUP BY dept_id;
explanation: GROUP BY dept_id groups rows by department, and COUNT(*) then counts rows within each group.

subject: dbms
title: Departments With More Than 5 Employees
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to return the dept_id of departments that have more than 5 employees.
sampleSolution: SELECT dept_id FROM Employees GROUP BY dept_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 5;
explanation: HAVING filters groups after aggregation (unlike WHERE, which can't reference COUNT()), keeping only groups with more than 5 rows.

subject: dbms
title: Highest Paid Employee in Each Department
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to return each department's id and its maximum salary.
sampleSolution: SELECT dept_id, MAX(salary) AS max_salary FROM Employees GROUP BY dept_id;
explanation: GROUP BY dept_id groups employees per department; MAX(salary) returns the highest salary within each group.

subject: dbms
title: Employee Names With Department Names
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list each employee's name along with the name of their department.
sampleSolution: SELECT e.name, d.dept_name FROM Employees e INNER JOIN Departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id;
explanation: An INNER JOIN matches each employee row to its department row using the dept_id foreign key relationship.

subject: dbms
title: Employees Including Those With No Department
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list every employee's name and their department name, including employees not currently assigned to any department (show NULL for department name in that case).
sampleSolution: SELECT e.name, d.dept_name FROM Employees e LEFT JOIN Departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id;
explanation: LEFT JOIN keeps every row from Employees even when there's no matching Departments row, filling dept_name with NULL for unmatched employees.

subject: dbms
title: Employees Who Earn More Than Their Manager
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list the names of employees who earn more than their own manager.
sampleSolution: SELECT e.name FROM Employees e JOIN Employees m ON e.manager_id = m.emp_id WHERE e.salary > m.salary;
explanation: This is a self join: the Employees table is joined to itself (aliased e and m) to compare each employee's salary against their manager's salary from the same table.

subject: dbms
title: Employees Earning Above Department Average
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list the names of employees whose salary is above the average salary of their own department.
sampleSolution: SELECT e.name FROM Employees e WHERE e.salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM Employees e2 WHERE e2.dept_id = e.dept_id);
explanation: This is a correlated subquery: for each outer row e, the subquery computes the average salary of just that employee's department (matched via dept_id) and compares against it.

subject: dbms
title: Employees Earning More Than the Company Average
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list the names of employees whose salary is greater than the overall average salary across the whole company.
sampleSolution: SELECT name FROM Employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM Employees);
explanation: The subquery computes a single company-wide average salary value (not correlated per-row), which the outer query then compares each employee's salary against.

subject: dbms
title: Top 3 Highest Paid Employees
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to return the names and salaries of the 3 highest-paid employees.
sampleSolution: SELECT name, salary FROM Employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 3;
explanation: ORDER BY salary DESC sorts from highest to lowest, and LIMIT 3 keeps only the first 3 rows of that sorted result.

subject: dbms
title: Rank Employees by Salary Within Each Department
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list each employee's name, department id, salary, and their salary rank within their own department (1 = highest paid in that department).
sampleSolution: SELECT name, dept_id, salary, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept_id ORDER BY salary DESC) AS salary_rank FROM Employees;
explanation: PARTITION BY dept_id resets the ranking for each department; RANK() OVER assigns a rank within each partition based on salary in descending order, so 1 is always the highest earner in that department.

subject: dbms
title: Give a 10% Raise to a Department
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to increase the salary of all employees in department 3 by 10%.
sampleSolution: UPDATE Employees SET salary = salary * 1.10 WHERE dept_id = 3;
explanation: UPDATE with WHERE dept_id = 3 restricts the change to only that department's employees, and salary * 1.10 applies a 10% increase to the current value.

subject: dbms
title: Delete Employees With No Department
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to delete all employees who don't currently have a department assigned (dept_id is NULL).
sampleSolution: DELETE FROM Employees WHERE dept_id IS NULL;
explanation: IS NULL is required (not = NULL) since NULL comparisons with = always evaluate to unknown, not true, in SQL.

subject: dbms
title: Second Highest Salary
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to return the second highest distinct salary in the company (return NULL if there isn't one).
sampleSolution: SELECT MAX(salary) AS second_highest FROM Employees WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employees);
explanation: The inner subquery finds the overall maximum salary; the outer query then finds the maximum salary strictly less than that, which is the second-highest distinct value.

subject: dbms
title: Departments With No Employees
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list the names of departments that currently have zero employees.
sampleSolution: SELECT d.dept_name FROM Departments d LEFT JOIN Employees e ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id WHERE e.emp_id IS NULL;
explanation: LEFT JOIN keeps every department even with no matching employees; filtering WHERE e.emp_id IS NULL isolates exactly the departments that had no match at all.

subject: dbms
title: Departments Where Average Salary Exceeds Company Average
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list the dept_id of departments whose average salary is higher than the overall company average salary.
sampleSolution: SELECT dept_id FROM Employees GROUP BY dept_id HAVING AVG(salary) > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM Employees);
explanation: GROUP BY computes each department's average via AVG(salary); HAVING then compares that per-group average against the company-wide average computed by the subquery.

subject: dbms
title: All Orders Above a Given Amount
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to list all order_id and amount for orders where the amount is greater than 500.
sampleSolution: SELECT order_id, amount FROM Orders WHERE amount > 500;
explanation: A simple WHERE filter comparing the amount column to the literal value 500.

subject: dbms
title: Total Revenue
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to return the total revenue across all orders (sum of amount).
sampleSolution: SELECT SUM(amount) AS total_revenue FROM Orders;
explanation: SUM() adds up the amount column across every row in the Orders table.

subject: dbms
title: Customer Names With Their Orders
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to list each order's order_id, order_date, and the name of the customer who placed it.
sampleSolution: SELECT o.order_id, o.order_date, c.name FROM Orders o JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id;
explanation: An INNER JOIN links each order to its customer row via the customer_id foreign key.

subject: dbms
title: Customers Who Have Never Ordered
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to list the names of customers who have never placed an order.
sampleSolution: SELECT c.name FROM Customers c LEFT JOIN Orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL;
explanation: LEFT JOIN keeps every customer even with no matching order; filtering on o.order_id IS NULL isolates customers with no order rows at all.

subject: dbms
title: Total Spend Per Customer
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to return each customer's customer_id and the total amount they've spent across all their orders.
sampleSolution: SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total_spent FROM Orders GROUP BY customer_id;
explanation: GROUP BY customer_id groups each customer's orders together, and SUM(amount) totals their spend within that group.

subject: dbms
title: Customers Who Spent More Than 10000 in Total
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to list the customer_id of customers whose total order amount across all their orders exceeds 10000.
sampleSolution: SELECT customer_id FROM Orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(amount) > 10000;
explanation: HAVING filters groups by an aggregate condition (SUM > 10000), which WHERE cannot do since it operates before aggregation.

subject: dbms
title: Best-Selling Product by Quantity
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to return the product_id and total quantity sold, for the single best-selling product across all orders.
sampleSolution: SELECT product_id, SUM(quantity) AS total_qty FROM OrderItems GROUP BY product_id ORDER BY total_qty DESC LIMIT 1;
explanation: GROUP BY product_id totals the quantity per product; sorting descending and taking LIMIT 1 isolates the single top-selling product.

subject: dbms
title: Revenue by Product Category
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to return the total revenue (sum of quantity * price) per product category.
sampleSolution: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS category_revenue FROM OrderItems oi JOIN Products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.category;
explanation: Joining OrderItems to Products brings in each item's price and category; multiplying quantity * price per row and summing per category via GROUP BY gives total revenue by category.

subject: dbms
title: Orders in a Specific Date Range
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to list all orders placed between '2024-01-01' and '2024-03-31' inclusive.
sampleSolution: SELECT * FROM Orders WHERE order_date BETWEEN '2024-01-01' AND '2024-03-31';
explanation: BETWEEN filters an inclusive range on order_date, equivalent to order_date >= '2024-01-01' AND order_date <= '2024-03-31'.

subject: dbms
title: Customers Who Ordered a Specific Product
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to list the distinct names of customers who have ordered a product named 'Laptop'.
sampleSolution: SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM Customers c JOIN Orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN OrderItems oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN Products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.product_name = 'Laptop';
explanation: This chains four tables together (Customers -> Orders -> OrderItems -> Products) to trace from a product name back to the customers who ordered it; DISTINCT avoids listing a customer more than once if they ordered it multiple times.

subject: dbms
title: Number of Orders Per Month
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to return the count of orders grouped by the month of order_date (assume a function EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date) is available).
sampleSolution: SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date) AS order_month, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM Orders GROUP BY EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date);
explanation: EXTRACT(MONTH FROM ...) pulls just the month component out of the date; grouping by that expression buckets orders into monthly counts regardless of year.

subject: dbms
title: Students With GPA Above 3.5
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list the names of students with a GPA greater than 3.5.
sampleSolution: SELECT name FROM Students WHERE gpa > 3.5;
explanation: A straightforward WHERE filter on the gpa column.

subject: dbms
title: Average GPA by Department
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to return each department and the average GPA of students in it.
sampleSolution: SELECT dept, AVG(gpa) AS avg_gpa FROM Students GROUP BY dept;
explanation: GROUP BY dept groups students by department, and AVG(gpa) computes the mean GPA within each group.

subject: dbms
title: Students Enrolled in a Specific Course
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list the names of students enrolled in the course named 'Database Systems'.
sampleSolution: SELECT s.name FROM Students s JOIN Enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id JOIN Courses c ON e.course_id = c.course_id WHERE c.course_name = 'Database Systems';
explanation: Joining Students to Enrollments to Courses traces from a course name back to enrolled students via the two foreign key relationships.

subject: dbms
title: Number of Students Per Course
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to return each course_id and the number of students enrolled in it.
sampleSolution: SELECT course_id, COUNT(*) AS enrolled_count FROM Enrollments GROUP BY course_id;
explanation: GROUP BY course_id groups enrollment rows by course, and COUNT(*) counts enrolled students within each group.

subject: dbms
title: Students Not Enrolled in Any Course
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list the names of students who are not currently enrolled in any course.
sampleSolution: SELECT s.name FROM Students s LEFT JOIN Enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id WHERE e.student_id IS NULL;
explanation: LEFT JOIN keeps every student even with no enrollment rows; filtering WHERE e.student_id IS NULL isolates students with zero matches.

subject: dbms
title: Students Enrolled in More Than 3 Courses
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list the student_id of students enrolled in more than 3 courses.
sampleSolution: SELECT student_id FROM Enrollments GROUP BY student_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 3;
explanation: GROUP BY student_id groups each student's enrollments; HAVING COUNT(*) > 3 keeps only students with more than 3 enrollment rows.

subject: dbms
title: Average Grade Points Per Semester
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to return the count of enrollments per semester, assuming the grade column stores letter grades (just count rows, not compute GPA).
sampleSolution: SELECT semester, COUNT(*) AS enrollment_count FROM Enrollments GROUP BY semester;
explanation: GROUP BY semester buckets enrollment rows by term, and COUNT(*) counts how many enrollments occurred in each.

subject: dbms
title: Students With the Highest GPA in Their Department
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list the names of students who have the highest GPA within their own department.
sampleSolution: SELECT s.name FROM Students s WHERE s.gpa = (SELECT MAX(s2.gpa) FROM Students s2 WHERE s2.dept = s.dept);
explanation: The correlated subquery finds the maximum GPA within the same department as the outer row; the outer WHERE keeps only students whose own GPA matches that department maximum (correctly including ties).

subject: dbms
title: Distinct Department IDs
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list the distinct dept_id values present in the Employees table.
sampleSolution: SELECT DISTINCT dept_id FROM Employees;
explanation: DISTINCT removes duplicate dept_id values so each department id appears only once, regardless of how many employees share it.

subject: dbms
title: Employees With No Manager
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list the names of employees who have no manager (manager_id is NULL).
sampleSolution: SELECT name FROM Employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL;
explanation: IS NULL correctly checks for a missing manager_id, since = NULL would not work in SQL.

subject: dbms
title: Minimum and Maximum Salary
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to return the minimum and maximum salary across all employees in one row.
sampleSolution: SELECT MIN(salary) AS min_salary, MAX(salary) AS max_salary FROM Employees;
explanation: MIN() and MAX() are both aggregate functions that can be computed together in a single SELECT over the whole table.

subject: dbms
title: Employees Sorted by Hire Date Descending
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list all employee names ordered from most recently hired to least recently hired.
sampleSolution: SELECT name FROM Employees ORDER BY hire_date DESC;
explanation: ORDER BY hire_date DESC sorts from the latest (most recent) date to the earliest.

subject: dbms
title: Managers and Their Direct Report Count
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list each manager's name and how many direct reports they have.
sampleSolution: SELECT m.name, COUNT(e.emp_id) AS direct_reports FROM Employees m JOIN Employees e ON e.manager_id = m.emp_id GROUP BY m.name;
explanation: This self join matches each manager row (m) to its direct reports (e) via manager_id, then GROUP BY m.name counts how many report rows matched each manager.

subject: dbms
title: Customers From a Specific City
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to list the names of customers located in 'Chennai'.
sampleSolution: SELECT name FROM Customers WHERE city = 'Chennai';
explanation: A simple equality filter on the city column.

subject: dbms
title: Number of Distinct Customers Who Ordered
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to return the count of distinct customers who have placed at least one order.
sampleSolution: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS customers_with_orders FROM Orders;
explanation: COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) counts each customer only once even if they have multiple orders.

subject: dbms
title: Average Order Value Per Customer, Above a Threshold
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to list the customer_id and average order amount for customers whose average order amount exceeds 1000.
sampleSolution: SELECT customer_id, AVG(amount) AS avg_order_value FROM Orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING AVG(amount) > 1000;
explanation: GROUP BY computes each customer's average order value; HAVING filters those group-level averages, which WHERE cannot do.

subject: dbms
title: Courses Worth More Than 3 Credits
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list the names of courses worth more than 3 credits.
sampleSolution: SELECT course_name FROM Courses WHERE credits > 3;
explanation: A direct filter on the credits column.

subject: dbms
title: Average GPA of Students Enrolled in a Specific Course
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to return the average GPA of students enrolled in the course named 'Data Structures'.
sampleSolution: SELECT AVG(s.gpa) AS avg_gpa FROM Students s JOIN Enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id JOIN Courses c ON e.course_id = c.course_id WHERE c.course_name = 'Data Structures';
explanation: Joining across all three tables narrows to students enrolled in that specific course, then AVG(s.gpa) computes their average GPA.

subject: dbms
title: Employees in a Specific Location
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list employee names whose department is located in 'Bangalore'.
sampleSolution: SELECT e.name FROM Employees e JOIN Departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id WHERE d.location = 'Bangalore';
explanation: Joining to Departments is needed since location lives there, not in Employees; WHERE then filters on that joined column.

subject: dbms
title: Employee Count by Location
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to return each department location and how many employees work there.
sampleSolution: SELECT d.location, COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM Employees e JOIN Departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id GROUP BY d.location;
explanation: After joining to bring in location, GROUP BY d.location aggregates employee counts per location (multiple departments could share a location).

subject: dbms
title: Categorize Employees by Salary Band
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list each employee's name and a salary band: 'High' if salary > 80000, 'Medium' if between 40000 and 80000 inclusive, otherwise 'Low'.
sampleSolution: SELECT name, CASE WHEN salary > 80000 THEN 'High' WHEN salary >= 40000 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Low' END AS salary_band FROM Employees;
explanation: CASE WHEN evaluates conditions top-to-bottom and returns the label for the first matching condition, falling to ELSE if none match.

subject: dbms
title: Running Total of Salaries by Hire Date
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list each employee's name, hire_date, and a running total of salary ordered by hire_date.
sampleSolution: SELECT name, hire_date, SUM(salary) OVER (ORDER BY hire_date) AS running_total FROM Employees;
explanation: A window function with SUM(...) OVER (ORDER BY hire_date) computes a cumulative sum as rows are processed in hire_date order, without collapsing rows the way GROUP BY would.

subject: dbms
title: Employees in the Department With the Most Employees
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list the names of employees who work in whichever department has the most employees.
sampleSolution: SELECT name FROM Employees WHERE dept_id = (SELECT dept_id FROM Employees GROUP BY dept_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1);
explanation: The subquery finds the single dept_id with the highest employee count; the outer query then lists employees belonging to that department.

subject: dbms
title: Employees With EXISTS Check
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query using EXISTS to list employee names who belong to a department that exists in the Departments table (i.e. exclude employees with an invalid/missing dept_id).
sampleSolution: SELECT name FROM Employees e WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Departments d WHERE d.dept_id = e.dept_id);
explanation: EXISTS checks whether the correlated subquery returns any row at all for each outer row, which is often more efficient than a JOIN when you only need existence, not the matched columns.

subject: dbms
title: Employee Names in Uppercase
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list every employee's name converted to uppercase.
sampleSolution: SELECT UPPER(name) AS name_upper FROM Employees;
explanation: UPPER() is a scalar string function applied to each row's name value independently.

subject: dbms
title: Years of Service
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list each employee's name and how many years they've been employed, computed from hire_date to the current date (assume a function like DATEDIFF or AGE is available per your SQL dialect; use a generic expression).
sampleSolution: SELECT name, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM AGE(CURRENT_DATE, hire_date)) AS years_of_service FROM Employees;
explanation: AGE(CURRENT_DATE, hire_date) computes the interval between today and hire_date, and EXTRACT(YEAR FROM ...) pulls out just the whole-year component.

subject: dbms
title: Employees Not in Specific Departments
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list employee names who are NOT in department 1, 2, or 3.
sampleSolution: SELECT name FROM Employees WHERE dept_id NOT IN (1, 2, 3);
explanation: NOT IN excludes rows whose dept_id matches any value in the given list.

subject: dbms
title: Employee Full Info With Column Aliases
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to select emp_id, name, and salary, renaming the output columns to id, employee_name, and monthly_salary respectively.
sampleSolution: SELECT emp_id AS id, name AS employee_name, salary AS monthly_salary FROM Employees;
explanation: AS renames a selected column in the result set without changing the underlying table's column name.

subject: dbms
title: Departments With Above-Average Headcount, Using a CTE
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Using a Common Table Expression (CTE), write a query to list dept_id and employee_count for departments whose employee_count is above the average employee_count across all departments.
sampleSolution: WITH dept_counts AS (SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM Employees GROUP BY dept_id) SELECT * FROM dept_counts WHERE employee_count > (SELECT AVG(employee_count) FROM dept_counts);
explanation: The CTE dept_counts precomputes per-department counts once, which the outer query then filters against the average of those same precomputed counts, avoiding recomputing the GROUP BY twice.

subject: dbms
title: Replace Missing Manager With a Default Label
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list each employee's name and their manager_id, showing 'No Manager' instead of NULL when manager_id is missing.
sampleSolution: SELECT name, COALESCE(CAST(manager_id AS VARCHAR), 'No Manager') AS manager_display FROM Employees;
explanation: COALESCE returns the first non-NULL argument, so it substitutes 'No Manager' only when manager_id is actually NULL.

subject: dbms
title: Total Salary Expenditure by Department, Sorted
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to return each dept_id and its total salary expenditure, ordered from highest to lowest total.
sampleSolution: SELECT dept_id, SUM(salary) AS total_salary FROM Employees GROUP BY dept_id ORDER BY total_salary DESC;
explanation: GROUP BY computes each department's total, and ORDER BY total_salary DESC then sorts those grouped results from highest spend to lowest.

subject: dbms
title: Categorize Orders by Size
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to list each order_id and a size label: 'Large' if amount > 1000, 'Medium' if between 300 and 1000 inclusive, otherwise 'Small'.
sampleSolution: SELECT order_id, CASE WHEN amount > 1000 THEN 'Large' WHEN amount >= 300 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Small' END AS order_size FROM Orders;
explanation: CASE WHEN checks conditions in order and returns the first matching label, falling through to ELSE for anything smaller.

subject: dbms
title: Rank Customers by Total Spend
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to list each customer_id, their total spend, and their spend rank (1 = highest spender).
sampleSolution: SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total_spend, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(amount) DESC) AS spend_rank FROM Orders GROUP BY customer_id;
explanation: GROUP BY first aggregates total spend per customer; RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ...) then ranks those aggregated totals across all customers.

subject: dbms
title: Products Never Ordered
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to list the product_name of products that have never appeared in any order.
sampleSolution: SELECT product_name FROM Products p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM OrderItems oi WHERE oi.product_id = p.product_id);
explanation: NOT EXISTS checks that the correlated subquery returns zero rows for a given product, meaning it never appears in OrderItems.

subject: dbms
title: Average Order Amount Overall
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to return the average order amount across all orders, rounded to 2 decimal places.
sampleSolution: SELECT ROUND(AVG(amount), 2) AS avg_order_amount FROM Orders;
explanation: AVG() computes the mean order amount, and ROUND(..., 2) formats it to 2 decimal places.

subject: dbms
title: Customers With Orders in Every Month of a Year
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to list customer_id values of customers who placed at least one order in every one of the 12 months of 2024 (assume EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date) is available).
sampleSolution: SELECT customer_id FROM Orders WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) = 2024 GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date)) = 12;
explanation: Filtering to 2024 orders, grouping per customer, and counting distinct months ensures only customers with orders spread across all 12 months are kept.

subject: dbms
title: Customers Who Ordered Specific Products
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to list distinct customer_id values for customers who have ordered a product with product_id in (101, 102, 103).
sampleSolution: SELECT DISTINCT o.customer_id FROM Orders o JOIN OrderItems oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE oi.product_id IN (101, 102, 103);
explanation: Joining Orders to OrderItems connects customers to the products in their orders; IN checks against the given list of product ids, and DISTINCT avoids duplicate customer listings.

subject: dbms
title: Customers Whose Name Starts With a Letter
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to list the names of customers whose name starts with 'A'.
sampleSolution: SELECT name FROM Customers WHERE name LIKE 'A%';
explanation: LIKE 'A%' matches any string starting with 'A' followed by any sequence of characters (including none).

subject: dbms
title: Top Spending Customer Per City, Using a CTE
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Using a CTE, write a query to find the top spending customer in each city (by total order amount).
sampleSolution: WITH spend AS (SELECT c.city, c.customer_id, c.name, SUM(o.amount) AS total_spend FROM Customers c JOIN Orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city, c.customer_id, c.name), ranked AS (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY total_spend DESC) AS rnk FROM spend) SELECT city, name, total_spend FROM ranked WHERE rnk = 1;
explanation: The first CTE aggregates total spend per customer; the second CTE ranks customers within each city using PARTITION BY; the outer query keeps only rank 1 (the top spender) per city.

subject: dbms
title: Orders With Missing Amount
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to list order_id values where the amount is missing (NULL).
sampleSolution: SELECT order_id FROM Orders WHERE amount IS NULL;
explanation: IS NULL is the correct way to test for a missing value, since = NULL never evaluates to true in SQL.

subject: dbms
title: Number of Products Per Category
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to return each category and how many distinct products fall into it.
sampleSolution: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM Products GROUP BY category;
explanation: GROUP BY category groups the Products table by category, and COUNT(*) counts rows (products) within each group.

subject: dbms
title: Classify Students by GPA
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list each student's name and a classification: 'Excellent' if gpa >= 3.7, 'Good' if gpa >= 3.0, otherwise 'Needs Improvement'.
sampleSolution: SELECT name, CASE WHEN gpa >= 3.7 THEN 'Excellent' WHEN gpa >= 3.0 THEN 'Good' ELSE 'Needs Improvement' END AS classification FROM Students;
explanation: CASE WHEN checks the GPA thresholds in order, from strictest to loosest, returning the first matching label.

subject: dbms
title: Rank Students by GPA Within Department
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list each student's name, dept, gpa, and their GPA rank within their own department (1 = highest GPA).
sampleSolution: SELECT name, dept, gpa, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY gpa DESC) AS gpa_rank FROM Students;
explanation: PARTITION BY dept resets the ranking separately for each department, and ORDER BY gpa DESC ranks 1 as the highest GPA within that partition.

subject: dbms
title: Courses With No Enrollments
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list the course_name of courses that currently have no students enrolled.
sampleSolution: SELECT course_name FROM Courses c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Enrollments e WHERE e.course_id = c.course_id);
explanation: NOT EXISTS confirms there is no matching row in Enrollments for that course_id, meaning nobody is enrolled.

subject: dbms
title: Total Credits Attempted Per Student
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to return each student_id and the total number of credits they've attempted across all their enrolled courses.
sampleSolution: SELECT e.student_id, SUM(c.credits) AS total_credits FROM Enrollments e JOIN Courses c ON e.course_id = c.course_id GROUP BY e.student_id;
explanation: Joining Enrollments to Courses brings in each course's credit value, and GROUP BY student_id sums those credits per student.

subject: dbms
title: Students Above Their Department's Average GPA, Using a CTE
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Using a CTE, write a query to list the names of students whose GPA is above their own department's average GPA.
sampleSolution: WITH dept_avg AS (SELECT dept, AVG(gpa) AS avg_gpa FROM Students GROUP BY dept) SELECT s.name FROM Students s JOIN dept_avg d ON s.dept = d.dept WHERE s.gpa > d.avg_gpa;
explanation: The CTE precomputes each department's average GPA once; the outer query joins each student back to their department's precomputed average and filters to those above it.

subject: dbms
title: Students Enrolled in Specific Courses
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list distinct student_id values of students enrolled in course_id 101 or 102.
sampleSolution: SELECT DISTINCT student_id FROM Enrollments WHERE course_id IN (101, 102);
explanation: IN checks course_id against the given list of values, and DISTINCT avoids listing the same student twice if enrolled in both.

subject: dbms
title: Course Names Containing a Keyword
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list course names that contain the word 'Data' anywhere in the name.
sampleSolution: SELECT course_name FROM Courses WHERE course_name LIKE '%Data%';
explanation: LIKE '%Data%' matches any string with 'Data' appearing anywhere, since % matches any sequence on both sides.

subject: dbms
title: Highest GPA Overall
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to return the highest GPA among all students.
sampleSolution: SELECT MAX(gpa) AS highest_gpa FROM Students;
explanation: MAX() returns the single largest value in the gpa column across the whole table.

subject: dbms
title: Failing Grades Count Per Student
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to return each student_id and how many courses they received a grade of 'F' in.
sampleSolution: SELECT student_id, COUNT(*) AS fail_count FROM Enrollments WHERE grade = 'F' GROUP BY student_id;
explanation: WHERE grade = 'F' filters to only failing enrollments before grouping, and GROUP BY student_id then counts how many such rows each student has.

subject: dbms
title: Students Enrolled in All Courses of a Given Department (Set-based)
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Assume Courses has a dept column matching Students.dept. Write a query to list students who are enrolled in every course offered in their own department.
sampleSolution: SELECT s.student_id, s.name FROM Students s WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT c.course_id FROM Courses c WHERE c.dept = s.dept AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Enrollments e WHERE e.student_id = s.student_id AND e.course_id = c.course_id));
explanation: This is a double-negation (relational division) pattern: it finds students for whom there is no course in their department that they have NOT enrolled in -- equivalent to 'enrolled in all of them'.

subject: dbms
title: Employee Count
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)

description: Write a query to count how many employees exist in the Employees table.

subject: dbms
title: List All Product Names

subject: dbms
title: List All Course Names
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list all course names in the Courses table.

subject: dbms
title: Employees With Salary in a Range
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list employee names with a salary between 40000 and 90000 inclusive.
sampleSolution: SELECT name FROM Employees WHERE salary BETWEEN 40000 AND 90000;
explanation: BETWEEN is inclusive on both ends, equivalent to salary >= 40000 AND salary <= 90000.

subject: dbms
title: Count of Distinct Managers
schema:

description: Write a query to return the number of distinct managers referenced in the Employees table.
sampleSolution: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT manager_id) AS distinct_managers FROM Employees;
explanation: COUNT(DISTINCT manager_id) counts unique manager_id values, ignoring NULLs and duplicates.

subject: dbms
title: Employees Who Manage More Than 2 People
schema:
Employees(emp_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept_id INT FK->Departments, salary DECIMAL, hire_date DATE, manager_id INT FK->Employees.emp_id)
Departments(dept_id INT PK, dept_name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list the names of employees who manage more than 2 other employees.
sampleSolution: SELECT name FROM Employees WHERE emp_id IN (SELECT manager_id FROM Employees GROUP BY manager_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 2);
explanation: The subquery finds manager_ids with more than 2 direct reports; the outer query then matches those ids back to the managers' own names.

description: Write a query to list the 5 most recent orders by order_date.
sampleSolution: SELECT * FROM Orders ORDER BY order_date DESC LIMIT 5;
explanation: Sorting by order_date descending puts the newest orders first, and LIMIT 5 keeps only the top 5.

subject: dbms
title: Products Priced Above Category Average
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)
Products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, category VARCHAR)
OrderItems(order_id INT FK->Orders, product_id INT FK->Products, quantity INT)
description: Write a query to list product_name for products priced above the average price within their own category.
sampleSolution: SELECT p.product_name FROM Products p WHERE p.price > (SELECT AVG(p2.price) FROM Products p2 WHERE p2.category = p.category);
explanation: The correlated subquery computes the average price within the same category as the outer row, and the outer WHERE keeps only products priced above that category average.

sampleSolution: SELECT name FROM Customers WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM signup_date) = 2023;

subject: dbms
title: Students With Perfect Attendance of A Grades
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to list the names of students who received a grade of 'A' in every course they are enrolled in (and are enrolled in at least one course).
sampleSolution: SELECT s.name FROM Students s JOIN Enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id GROUP BY s.student_id, s.name HAVING COUNT(*) = SUM(CASE WHEN e.grade = 'A' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END);
explanation: GROUP BY groups each student's enrollments; HAVING compares the total enrollment count to the count of 'A' grades (via a conditional SUM), keeping only students where every single enrollment was an A.

subject: dbms
title: Cumulative Revenue Over Time
schema:
Customers(customer_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, signup_date DATE)
Orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK->Customers, order_date DATE, amount DECIMAL)

description: Write a query to list each order_id, order_date, and a running cumulative total of revenue ordered by order_date.
sampleSolution: SELECT order_id, order_date, SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY order_date) AS cumulative_revenue FROM Orders;
explanation: The window function SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY order_date) computes a running total as rows are processed in date order, without collapsing individual order rows.

subject: dbms
title: Average Credits Per Department
schema:
Students(student_id INT PK, name VARCHAR, dept VARCHAR, gpa DECIMAL)
Courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT)
Enrollments(student_id INT FK->Students, course_id INT FK->Courses, grade VARCHAR, semester VARCHAR)
description: Write a query to return each department and the average number of credits its enrolled students are taking, based on completed enrollments.
sampleSolution: SELECT s.dept, AVG(c.credits) AS avg_credits FROM Students s JOIN Enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id JOIN Courses c ON e.course_id = c.course_id GROUP BY s.dept;
explanation: Joining Students to Enrollments to Courses brings each enrollment's credit value together with the student's department, and GROUP BY dept averages those credits per department.
